patents_audited.title: A vascular filter
patents_audited.independent_claim_1_text: A vascular filter (300, 340) comprising:- capture members (3, 121) for capturing thrombus passing through a blood vessel; wherein the capture members (3) are movable between a capturing configuration and an open configuration; and wherein the filter comprises a holder member (331, 342) to hold the capture members in the capturing configuration; support members for supporting the capture members relative to a wall of a blood vessel, characterized in that the support members comprise: a proximal first support member (302) configured to extend circumferentially around a wall of a blood vessel; a distal second support member (312) configured to extend circumferentially around the wall of a blood vessel; a third support member (303) configured to extend along the wall of the blood vessel and connecting the first support member to the second support member; wherein a proximal end of the first support member (302) is located proximally of a proximal end of the capture members (3) and a distal end of the distal support member (312) is located distally of a distal end of the capture members.

dependent_claims_with_keywords.text: A vascular filter as claimed in claim 1, wherein the holder member (342) is biodegradable and/or bioabsorbable.

A vascular filter as claimed in claim 2, wherein the holder member comprises a suture (342) extending through an opening (342) at a distal end of each capture member (121) to hold the capture members in a capturing configuration, and wherein a knot is tied around one capture member such that once the suture breaks at a point away from the knot the suture releases the capture members and stays attached to said capture member.

A vascular filter as claimed in any preceding claim, wherein the filter comprises anchor barb elements (301) on at least one support member (303) configured to be embedded at least partially into a wall of a blood vessel.
A vascular filter as claimed in any preceding claim, wherein at least part of the anchor barb elements (301) are biodegradable and/or bioabsorbable.
A vascular filter as claimed in claim 17, wherein the tensioning members are connected to the capture members by connecting members (305) which are biodegradable and/or bioabsorbable.

specification_key_passages.text: The Nitinol frame is a single component which comprises zigzag type design features called 'crowns' 302, 312 at both its ends. This design allows the device 300 to be crimped or reduced in diameter so that it can be delivered through the vascular system in a catheter of much smaller diameter than the vena cava 4.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Nitinol used for SELF-EXPANDING DELIVERY, not thermally-triggered retrieval.

specification_key_passages.text: In another embodiment the support member comprises an anchor member. The anchor member may be configured to be embedded at least partially into a wall of a blood vessel. The anchor member may comprise a barb element. The anchor member may be configured to be removed from a wall of a blood vessel upon application of a [force].
specification_key_passages.relevance: Anchor barbs can be biodegradable; no thermal trigger mentioned.

specification_key_passages.text: The filter can be used either permanently, or temporarily with subsequent retrieval or conversion for PE prevention. If the filter is left in place, it functions as a permanent IVC filter. Alternatively, the filters may be retrieved once the duration of PE prophylaxis has been achieved.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Retrieval is acknowledged as a clinical use case but no thermal-triggered SMA release mechanism described.

specification_key_passages.text: Referring to Figs. 60 to 63 there is illustrated another vascular filter assembly. The vascular filter assembly comprises a vascular filter 200 and a retrieval catheter 202 for retrieving the filter 200 from a location in the inferior vena cava 4.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Retrieval catheter is a mechanical device; no thermal/SMA element.

specification_key_passages.text: The shape memory of the capture arms 121 are configured to remember a tubular shape. The only biodegradable element of the filter 120 is the holder 122 at the apex 6 of the filter 120.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Shape memory is for capture-arm geometry retention (deployment), NOT for thermally-triggered release for retrieval.

patents_audited.verdict_rationale: EP2043551B1 is an IVC filter with biodegradable holder/suture/anchor elements that mechanically release (via suture breakage) for timed retrieval. It teaches (a) Nitinol as a frame material, (b) shape memory as a deployment-geometry mechanism, (c) biodegradable elements for timed mechanical release. It does NOT teach (i) thermal-triggered SMA phase-transition release, (ii) thermal isolation to protect surrounding tissue, or (iii) electrothermal activation. The M3_REFINED candidate's THERMAL ISOLATION element specifically is NOT disclosed. The bioabsorbable suture/holder mechanism (claims 2, 8, 12, 18) is a TIMED MECHANICAL release, not a thermal one. NOVELTY DISTINCTION: M3_REFINED requires ELECTROTHERMAL phase-transition activation with THERMAL ISOLATION — neither element is present in EP2043551B1. However, this patent DOES teach biodegradable timed-release which is closer to M4 (the alternative candidate).

patents_audited.title: Vascular remodeling device
patents_audited.independent_claim_1_text: A device for removing a clot from a blood vessel, the device comprising: a proximal section having a plurality of first cells, each of the first cells defined by first sidewalls and at least some of the first sidewalls are curved, wherein the proximal section comprises a tapered portion and a body portion distal of the tapered portion, and wherein, the body portion of the proximal section includes a plurality of forward free peaks, a plurality of forward connected peaks, a plurality of reverse connected peaks, and does not include any reverse free peaks, and the body portion comprises at least three longitudinally aligned forward free peaks spaced apart around a circumference of the device; and a distal section coupled to the proximal section such that the body portion of the proximal section is between the tapered portion of the proximal section and the distal section along a length of the device, the distal section having a plurality of second cells, each of the second cells defined by second sidewalls, wherein the plurality of first cells and the plurality of second cells include a plurality of six-sided cells and a plurality of four-sided cells, and wherein the proximal section and the distal section are connected by an intermediate section extending between the proximal section and the distal section, the intermediate section comprising at least one strut extending parallel to a central longitudinal axis of the device.

dependent_claims_with_keywords.text: The device of claim 1, wherein the proximal section, the distal section, and the intermediate section are cut from the same tube or sheet of material and then re-shaped via heat treatment.
The device of claim 1, wherein at least a portion of the device includes Nitinol or cobalt-chromium ('CoCr').
The device of claim 1, wherein the device is self-expanding.

specification_key_passages.text: In some embodiments, the device 50 comprises a self-expanding (e.g., super elastic, CoCr alloy, polyglycolic acid, polylactic acid, etc.) and/or a shape-memory material (e.g., Nitinol, shape memory polymers, etc.), thereby causing the device 50 to be self-expanding under certain conditions (e.g., no [external] constraint).
specification_key_passages.relevance: Shape-memory/Nitinol used for SELF-EXPANDING DEPLOYMENT (passive, body-temperature triggered). NO thermal-triggered release.

specification_key_passages.text: According to some embodiments, a method of retrieving a clot from a vessel comprises advancing a catheter in the vessel distal to the clot, the catheter at least partially containing a device in a compressed state, the device including a proximal section and a distal section; deploying the device from the catheter...
specification_key_passages.relevance: Retrieval here refers to CLOT retrieval (the device retrieves a clot), NOT retrieval of the device itself.

specification_key_passages.text: The proximal portion has an open cell design, a closed cell design, or a hybrid cell design having no reverse free-peaks for retrievability, good flexibility, and scaffold opening area.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Device is designed to be retrievable (no reverse free-peaks) but the mechanism is mechanical pull-back through catheter, NOT thermal/SMA-triggered release.

patents_audited.verdict_rationale: US11690741B2 is a vascular remodeling device (stent-like clot retriever) for aneurysm bifurcation treatment. Claim 1 is entirely a GEOMETRY claim (cell shapes, peak configurations) for clot retrieval device geometry, with no thermal/SMA release mechanism. Nitinol/shape-memory appear only as MATERIAL options for SELF-EXPANDING deployment (passive, body-temperature triggered). The 'retrieval' here is the device retrieving a CLOT, not retrieval of the device itself. Does NOT teach thermal-isolated SMA release for late-stage retrieval of an anchored implant. NO direct relevance to M3_REFINED.

patents_audited.title: Anchors with Biodegradable Constraints
patents_audited.assignee: GI Dynamics Inc (current: Morphic Medical Inc)
patents_audited.independent_claim_1_text: An implant comprising: a cylindrical, collapsible anchor to be deployed within a lumen; a protrusion coupled to the anchor, the protrusion, in a constrained state, extending from an exterior surface of the anchor and, in an unconstrained state, extending further from the exterior surface of the anchor; and a biodegradable constraint configured to maintain the protrusion in the constrained state until the constraint releases.
patents_audited.independent_claim_42_text: A method of securing a collapsible anchor within a lumen, the method comprising: deploying the cylindrical, collapsible anchor within the lumen, the collapsible anchor having a protrusion that, in a constrained state, extends from an exterior surface of the anchor; maintaining the protrusion in the constrained state with a biodegradable constraint; and penetrating a wall of the lumen with the protrusion in the constrained state to secure the anchor.
patents_audited.independent_claim_56_text: An implant comprising: a collapsible anchor to be deployed within a lumen; a bi-directional barb coupled to the anchor, the barb, in a constrained state, extending from an exterior surface of the anchor and, in an unconstrained state, extending further from the exterior surface of the anchor; and a biodegradable constraint configured to maintain the barb in the constrained state until the constraint releases.

dependent_claims_with_keywords.text: The implant of claim 1, wherein the constraint degrades when exposed to water.
The implant of claim 1, wherein the constraint degrades when exposed to acid.
The implant of claim 1, wherein the constraint is bioresorbable.

The implant of claim 1, further comprising additional biodegradable constraints, each constraint configured to maintain the protrusion in a different constrained state and to degrade over a different predetermined period after the implant has been deployed within the lumen.
The implant of claim 1, wherein the protrusion is a bi-directional barb.

The method of claim 42, further comprising: allowing the biodegradable constraint to degrade over a predetermined period after the implant has been deployed in the lumen to release the protrusion from the constrained state.
The method of claim 45, wherein the period is selected to allow the tissue to grow.
The method of claim 42, wherein penetrating the wall of the lumen includes allowing tissue to grow about the open loop.
The method of claim 52, further comprising: collapsing the helix with a drawstring; and withdrawing the collapsible anchor from the lumen.

specification_key_passages.text: Embodiments of the present invention provide improved anchoring of an implant in the gastrointestinal tract and can increase the duration that an implant can be anchored in the intestine by providing biodegradable constraints that maintain anchoring protrusions in a constrained state until the constraint releases.
specification_key_passages.relevance: PATENT'S CORE MECHANISM: biodegradable constraint maintains protrusion in CONSTRAINED state until release. After release, protrusion EXTENDS FURTHER (more anchoring).

specification_key_passages.text: Protrusions with open loops ... can secure an implant for longer periods of time while minimizing the risk of damage to nearby organs. In addition, protrusions or barbs can be deployed in a constrained state, e.g. having reduced barb height, to initially secure the anchor in the wall of the duodenum, and the barb can then extend to its full length to increase the holding power.
specification_key_passages.relevance: DIRECTION IS OPPOSITE TO M4: degradation INCREASES anchoring (more holding power), not decreases. M4 (CereVasc idea) would use resorption to DECREASE anchoring for easy retrieval.

specification_key_passages.text: Allowing tissue to grow about the protrusion.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Patent explicitly teaches TISSUE INGROWTH AROUND PROTRUSION as the anchoring mechanism. The retrieval method (drawstring + collapsing helix) is mechanical, NOT thermal.

specification_key_passages.text: Preferably, protrusion 710 is a bidirectional barb constructed of a shape memory alloy (e.g., Nitinol or similar) with a compound angle shape set into the barb. A releasable restraining mechanism, such as biodegradable constraint 714, allows the compound barb to change height over a predetermined period of time in the body.
specification_key_passages.relevance: CRITICAL: combines shape-memory alloy (Nitinol) with biodegradable constraint. But the release mechanism is BIODEGRADATION, not THERMAL activation. Shape memory here is for barb geometry retention.

specification_key_passages.text: An implant secured with protrusions tipped with open loops or barbs may be removed laparoscopically, surgically, or, more preferably, endoscopically with an endoscope. For example, an implant may be collapsed using a drawstring, then withdrawn from the intestine using an endoscope.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Retrieval is mechanical (drawstring + endoscope). NO thermal activation.

patents_audited.verdict_rationale: US20110276091A1 is a CRITICAL NEAR-NEIGHBOR for M4 (biodegradable timed-release anchor) but NOT a DIRECT_HIT on M3_REFINED. Key distinctions: (1) GI Dynamics teaches biodegradable constraint that releases a protrusion to EXTEND FURTHER OUTWARD (more anchoring) — M4 wants the opposite (constraint releases to DECREASE anchoring for easy retrieval). (2) GI Dynamics teaches retrieval via MECHANICAL DRAWSTRING + endoscope, NOT thermal-triggered SMA release. (3) GI Dynamics mentions shape-memory alloy (Nitinol) but as a material for barb geometry, not for thermal-triggered phase transition. (4) GI Dynamics is in the GASTROINTESTINAL tract (duodenal implants), not the cerebrovascular/CSF-venous context. M3_REFINED (thermal-isolated SMA release) is NOT directly anticipated. M4 (biodegradable timed-retrieval-window) has STRONGER overlap — M4 may be OBVIOUS in light of US20110276091A1 because both use biodegradable degradation to TIME a release event for an anchored implant. M4 survives only if the directional inversion (release-to-anchor LESS vs release-to-anchor MORE) and the cerebrovascular context provide a non-obvious distinction. PATENT COUNSEL OPINION REQUIRED for M4.

patents_audited.title: Heart anchor device
patents_audited.independent_claim_14_text: A method for delivering a shunt at an atrial septum of a patient, the method comprising: advancing a sheath percutaneously through the atrial septum to position a distal end of the sheath in a first atrium; moving the sheath proximally relative to a core within a lumen of the sheath such that a first expandable end of the shunt extends distally out the distal end of the sheath and transitions from a contracted state within the lumen of the sheath to an expanded state in the first atrium; moving the sheath proximally relative to the core such that a second expandable end of the shunt extends distally out the distal end of the sheath and disengages with one or more protrusions of the core to transition from a contracted state within the lumen of the sheath to an expanded state in a second atrium.

dependent_claims_with_keywords.text: The method of claim 15, wherein the first and second pluralities of arms each comprise petals configured to be released separately.

specification_key_passages.text: Alternatively to tube 505 allowing flap 138 and arm 135 to exit once it is pushed out of channel 500, other triggers may be required to cause tube 505 to allow flap 138 to be released. For example, tube 505 may be made from a stiff material which softens when cooled or heated. When it is desired to release flap 138, the tube 505 is heated or cooled in order to release the flap unit. Alternatively [other triggers may be used].
specification_key_passages.relevance: CRITICAL PASSAGE: patent mentions THERMAL TRIGGER (heating/cooling to soften tube) as ONE OF SEVERAL ALTERNATIVE TRIGGERS for releasing a flap unit. BUT: this is for DEPLOYMENT (releasing flap from delivery tube), NOT for late-stage RETRIEVAL after tissue ingrowth. Also: thermal softening of polymer tube, not SMA phase transition.

specification_key_passages.text: FIG. 18 is a schematic illustration of an anchor device 100 with a retrieval string 801, in accordance with an exemplary embodiment of the invention. A retrieval string 801 connects distal points 118 of petals 104A to a central junction 802. If necessary, a hook 810 is passed through a working channel of the delivery device, or is otherwise brought to central junction 802 and is pulled proximally.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Retrieval is MECHANICAL (string + hook + proximal pull). NO thermal trigger.

specification_key_passages.text: Optionally, in embodiments in which an anchoring device carries a closure portion 198, retrieval string 801 is connected to closure portion 198. Optionally, in embodiments including flap 138, a same string is used for restricting movements of the flap (wire 149, FIG. 4A) and for retrieval.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Confirms mechanical retrieval mechanism.

specification_key_passages.text: An aspect of some embodiments of the present invention relates to a method of closing an orifice in a body organ. The method includes implanting in the orifice a valve including a bio-degradable material which maintains the valve in an open position or in a state in which it may open and close. As the bio-degradable material dissolves or after it dissolves, the valve changes to a permanently closed [state].
specification_key_passages.relevance: Bio-degradable material used for timed VALVE CLOSURE (orifice closure), NOT for anchor release or retrieval.

patents_audited.verdict_rationale: US20190328513A1 (V-Wave) is an inter-atrial septum shunt for heart failure treatment. The thermal trigger passage (p-0345) is the closest near-neighbor to M3_REFINED across all 5 patents, but it is a DEPLOYMENT release (flap unit release from delivery tube via polymer softening), NOT a late-stage RETRIEVAL release after tissue ingrowth. Critical distinctions: (1) The thermal trigger is for polymer tube softening, NOT SMA phase transition. (2) The release is for DEPLOYMENT from delivery tool, NOT for retrieval of a chronically implanted device. (3) No thermal isolation element to protect surrounding tissue. (4) Retrieval is mechanical (retrieval string + hook). (5) Different anatomical context (atrial septum vs CSF-venous). M3_REFINED (thermal-isolated SMA release for late-stage retrieval after tissue ingrowth) is NOT directly anticipated. The patent does demonstrate that thermal triggers for release are KNOWN in the art of implantable shunt devices — this WEAKENS the non-obviousness argument for M3_REFINED's thermal trigger element.

patents_audited.title: Systems for establishing retrograde carotid arterial blood flow
patents_audited.independent_claim_1_text: An interventional catheter system for treating a blood vessel, comprising: an arterial access device (110) comprising: a distal sheath (605) that can be introduced into a common carotid artery; characterized by a flow line (605) connected to and forming a first leg of a retrograde shunt (120), the flow line being fluidly connected to the transcervical access sheath by a Y-connector (620); a tube (705) coaxially positioned over an exterior of the transcervical access sheath (605) and having a proximal end (710) that engages the Y-connector (620), wherein a length of the tube (705) limits introduction of the sheath (605) into the common carotid artery to an exposed distal portion of the sheath (605); and a transcervical, interventional catheter comprising: an elongate shaft (2310) sized for insertion in a common carotid artery; an expandable dilation member (3110) coupled to a distal region of the elongate shaft, the expandable dilation member adapted to expand outward; a stent containment member (2305) positioned over the elongate shaft and the stent to contain a stent in a collapsed state; and a control mechanism (2207) adapted to retract the stent containment member relative to the elongate shaft, wherein the control mechanism is adapted to retract the stent containment member from the elongate shaft; wherein the interventional catheter has a working length of approximately 40 cm to 75 cm.

specification_key_passages.text: The disclosed systems and methods may employ a wide variety of self-closing elements, typically being mechanical elements which include an anchor portion and a self-closing portion. The anchor portion may comprise hooks, pins, staples, clips, tine, suture, or the like, which are engaged in the exterior [of the artery]. Optionally, the self-closing portion is bio-absorbable.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Anchor here is for artery-wall closure (self-closing element for the puncture site), NOT for the implant being retrieved. Bio-absorbable is for closure timing, not retrieval.

specification_key_passages.text: A self-closing element may be deployed about the penetration in the wall of the common carotid artery prior to withdrawing the sheath 605 at the end of the procedure.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Self-closing element is deployed AT END of procedure to close artery puncture. NO retrieval mechanism for a chronically implanted device.

specification_key_passages.text: In carotid stenting procedures, adjunct embolic protection devices are usually used to at least partially alleviate the risk of emboli. The primary category of embolic protection devices is distal filters. These filters are positioned in the internal carotid artery distal to the region of stenting.
specification_key_passages.relevance: Mentions embolic protection devices (filters) but no SMA/thermal release.

patents_audited.verdict_rationale: EP3789069B1 is about establishing retrograde carotid arterial blood flow during carotid artery stenting. The patent is entirely about FLOW REVERSAL for embolic protection during acute interventional procedures, not about RETRIEVAL of a chronically implanted device. No SMA, no thermal trigger, no shape-memory release mechanism. The 'anchor' mentioned is for artery-wall closure (self-closing puncture-closure element), not implant retrieval. This patent is irrelevant to M3_REFINED and is only weakly related to M5 (flow reversal flush) which was already dropped in V1.

summary_table.teaches_thermal_SMA_release: NO (SMA mentioned but for barb geometry)
summary_table.teaches_late_retrieval_release: PARTIAL — biodegradable timed constraint release (OPPOSITE direction: more anchoring)

summary_table.teaches_thermal_SMA_release: PARTIAL — thermal polymer softening for DEPLOYMENT release (not retrieval, not SMA)

CONDITIONS_for_survival: M3_REFINED must claim ELECTROTHERMAL SMA phase-transition activation (not just polymer softening) — distinguishes over US20190328513A1 (V-Wave) which teaches thermal polymer softening for deployment.
M3_REFINED must claim THERMAL ISOLATION element explicitly — NONE of the 5 patents teach thermal isolation to protect surrounding tissue.

M3_REFINED must claim use for LATE-STAGE RETRIEVAL AFTER TISSUE INGROWTH — distinguishes over US20190328513A1 (deployment only) and US20110276091A1 (constraint release for additional anchoring, opposite direction).

M3_REFINED must claim the CEREBROVASCULAR / CSF-VENOUS context — distinguishes over IVC filter (EP2043551B1), cardiovascular aneurysm (US11690741B2), GI tract (US20110276091A1), and atrial septum (US20190328513A1).
WEAKNESSES_identified: Thermal-triggered release as a CONCEPT is taught by US20190328513A1 (V-Wave) for polymer softening — the non-obviousness of the thermal-trigger element itself is WEAKENED.
Biodegradable timed-release is taught by EP2043551B1 (Novate) and US20110276091A1 (Gi Dynamics) — alternative non-thermal mechanisms are well-established.
SMA + biodegradable constraint combination is taught by US20110276091A1 (Gi Dynamics, p-0074) — though not for thermal-triggered release, the material combination is not novel.
Tissue ingrowth as a retrieval challenge is acknowledged in US20110276091A1 (claim 46, claim 50) — though for opposite-direction mechanism.
implications_for_M3_REFINED.OVERALL_V2_ASSESSMENT: M3_REFINED survives V2 passage audit. NO DIRECT_HIT found. Three NEIGHBORING_PROBLEM patents require careful claim drafting to distinguish over. The THERMAL ISOLATION element is the load-bearing novel feature — it is NOT taught by any of the 5 patents.

implications_for_M4_alternative.M4_CONDITIONAL_SURVIVAL: M4 (biodegradable timed-retrieval-window) is the most threatened by US20110276091A1 (Gi Dynamics). Gi Dynamics teaches biodegradable constraint that releases a protrusion to extend FURTHER OUTWARD (more anchoring), which is the OPPOSITE direction of M4 (release to DECREASE anchoring for easy retrieval). The directional inversion is a potential §103 non-obviousness argument. The cerebrovascular context (vs GI tract) provides additional distinction. PATENT COUNSEL OPINION REQUIRED for M4.

honest_negative_results: M3 basic mechanism (SMA release for vascular implant) is NOT novel — confirmed by 4 of 5 patents mentioning Nitinol/shape-memory.
Thermal-triggered release as a CONCEPT is not novel — V-Wave (US20190328513A1) teaches thermal polymer softening for deployment release.
Tissue ingrowth as a retrieval challenge is acknowledged in the prior art (Gi Dynamics claim 46).
The 5 patents were not all DIRECT_HITS as feared — only 0 of 5 are DIRECT_HITS. 3 are NEIGHBORING_PROBLEM, 2 are NOT_RELEVANT.
search_completeness_rationale: All 5 patents fetched from Google Patents with full claim text + specification passage extraction. Biblio data (assignee, inventors, filing/grant dates) confirmed via application-timeline events. Keyword scan complete for 18 keywords across all claims and descriptions. PatentBear free web search was not used because Google Patents direct fetch provides equivalent (better) coverage.
